rationale: C08 is the closest because it is another recent proclamation inviting participation in a nationally significant event, while C21 and C14 likewise urge participation or observance. But the overlap is limited to generic proclamation structure and routine invitational language. None shares the child's distinctive machinery: quotation of a joint resolution authorizing invitations, recital of invitations already extended by a governor through the Department of State and overseas missions, and an invitation directed jointly to the States and foreign nations to participate in a specific international trade fair.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby invite and urge the States of the Union and foreign nations to participate to the fullest practicable extent
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby invite American citizens from every region of our country to come to their Nation's Capital and participate
shared_material.explanation: C08 shares an invitation-to-participate formulation, but this is generic ceremonial language and lacks the child's specific international and intergovernmental mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby invite and urge ... to participate
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I invite the Governors of the States, Territories, and possessions of the United States to issue proclamations for the same purpose. I also urge ... all interested agencies and individuals to unite
shared_material.explanation: C21 combines invitation and exhortation, but for a recurring observance and without a materially parallel operative scheme.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: do urge all our citizens to participate in appropriate ceremonies and celebrations
shared_material.explanation: C14 has similar exhortatory language, but only at the level of a routine public-observance proclamation.
